extracted.intended_audience: AI researchers, developers, and creative authors exploring multimodal LLM capabilities
extracted.subtask_description: Produce a one‑page graphic novel for a young‑girl audience: plan panel layout, write dialogue/captions, design characters/backgrounds, ink & color, and apply lettering. The page gives concrete stepwise guidance and examples plus related multimodal/code generation constraints for image/svg/3D outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page layout / panel flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Sketch out a rough layout of the page, dividing it into panels of different sizes and shapes according to the flow of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: use a large panel for the opening scene (girl drawing), smaller panels for discovery/middle beats, and a final large panel for the ending hug scene. Choose panel sizes and arrangement to support pacing and emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue and captions (writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the dialogue and captions for each panel, using simple and expressive language that matches the tone and mood of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of speech: 'Wow, what a cool crayon!', 'I wish I had a unicorn friend', 'You’re real!'. Use captions to introduce setting/voice. Include sound effects (e.g., 'Scribble, scribble', 'Poof!') to add drama and humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character and background design (visual style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw the characters and backgrounds for each panel, using a clear and colorful style that appeals to little girls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the girl cute and expressive (big eyes, long hair, a dress), and the unicorn majestic and friendly (horn, mane, tail). Add distinguishing details (flower in hair, star on forehead, a poster) to make characters unique and interesting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inking and coloring technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Ink and color the panels, using a pen, a brush, or a digital tool to outline and fill in the shapes and textures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use black ink for outlines and bright colors for characters and backgrounds (e.g., pink, purple, blue). Apply shading, highlights and patterns (gradients, sparkles, stripes) to create depth and contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lettering and caption placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the dialogue and captions, using a font, a lettering, or a handwriting that fits the style and voice of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use round/bubbly fonts for speech and a script/elegant font for captions; place text in speech balloons and caption boxes sized to match panels. Use emphasis (bold/italic/size/color) to highlight words or emotions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only basic shapes / no external images or textures
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompts/requirements for generated images/code specify that extern images and textures are not allowed; only basic shapes and plain colors should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple examples state: 'You are not allow to use extern images, textures but only basic shapes.' and 'The HTML file cannot use any external image or any texture, just plain colors.' This is an explicit production constraint for SVG/HTML/three.js outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kandinsky-style random image generator constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Design a random Kandinsky painting generator using basic canvas drawing primitives and random parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show: set canvas size, choose random pastel/background color, clear canvas, draw a random number of shapes (e.g., 10–20), shape types include circle/rectangle/triangle/line, choose random positions/sizes/colors, fill or stroke shapes. Include a UI control (button) to regenerate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3D scene / three.js production constraints and layout requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For 3D HTML/three.js model generation, the scene must obey explicit structural, color, connectivity, and asset constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated constraints include: no external images/textures (plain colors only); arrange islands like the Olympic rings; ensure island colors match Olympic ring colors and are positioned horizontally; redesign which islands are connected by bridges; add multiple dragons with different colors, heights and trajectories (each dragon must use only one color); add a special island opposite the yellow island that is not created by the standard 'createIsland' routine and resembles the 'End Island' with an End City on top. These are concrete acceptance criteria for the generated 3D scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: SVG/TikZ letter-composed character constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce code (TikZ/SVG) that composes a person from alphabet letters: arms and torso Y, face O (add facial features), legs using H's legs; include clothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prompt explicitly requests adding a shirt and pants and using letters as the building blocks. The output should follow the letter mappings and include additional features as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter-object combination output format and shape constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: When given an object name and a letter, first produce a one-line description of how the object can be combined with the letter, then produce SVG code using basic shapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SVG should use shapes like ellipses, triangles and polygons and avoid using quadratic curves. The prompt shows multiple rounds (pig+H, house+U, chair+K, dog+Q, car+E) as examples of the required format: one-line description followed by SVG code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative revision / follow explicit change list
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept and apply incremental user requests to modify generated images/code (e.g., add roof, cover text with object, add wheels, change grass color, add characters, add or recolor elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of requested edits: 'Can you add more details? Add a roof to the bank. Make sure all the text on the top layer, it is covered by some object now. Add 2 wheels to the car. Make the grass red. Add a woman on the right of the teller. Add a big red frog on the top left of the green frog.' The generator is expected to implement such specific, ordered changes.
